source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 3 (ISL A3) · lesson 22. Rewritten for children from Dr. Hassan's lesson; facts and references kept.

learn.en: In the Cave of Ḥirāʾ, the angel Jibrīl came and said: “Read!” The Prophet ﷺ said: “I am not a reader.” This happened three times.
learn.title: “Read!”

learn.en: Then the angel recited: “Read in the name of your Lord who created — created man from a clinging clot. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous — who taught by the pen — taught man what he did not know.” (Qur'an 96:1–5)
learn.title: The first verses

learn.en: This was the beginning of waḥy — revelation. It was in Ramadan, when the Prophet ﷺ was forty years old.
learn.title: The beginning

learn.en: He came home trembling and said to Khadījah: “Cover me! Cover me!” She covered him until his fear went away. (Bukhari 3)
learn.title: “Cover me!”

learn.en: The first word of the Qur'an is “Read” — a call to learn! And learning starts “in the name of your Lord”.
learn.title: A call to learn

quiz.en: What was the first word Jibrīl said?
In which month did the first revelation come?
True or false? The Prophet ﷺ was forty years old.
True or false? The first verses mention the pen.

think.q: The Qur'an starts with “Read!”. What is something you want to learn this month?
think.a: Maybe a new surah, reading Arabic, or a new skill — say Bismillāh and start!

parents.summary: In Ḥirāʾ, in Ramadan, Jibrīl brought the first verses: “Read in the name of your Lord…” (96:1–5). Islam begins with a call to learn.
parents.tip: Read a page of a good book together and say Bismillāh before starting.
